checks.title: Order feature the venue does not hold
checks.description: The scenario's decision logic declares an order feature its venue's API does not hold, and its scenario set declares no exception for it.

checks.title: Order features not declared
checks.description: The scenario's decision logic does not say which order features it uses.

checks.title: Exception nothing needs
checks.description: The scenario set declares an order feature as beyond its venue that no scenario needs, or that the venue holds anyway.

checks.title: Order features beyond the venue
checks.description: The run used order features its venue's API does not hold, as its scenario set declared.

checks.title: Scenario without a name
checks.description: A scenario in the set has no name.

checks.title: Duplicate scenario name
checks.description: Two or more scenarios in the set share a name; every copy is refused.

checks.title: No end to the scenario
checks.description: The scenario sets neither an end date nor a tick limit, so nothing says where it stops.

checks.title: Invalid date range
checks.description: The scenario's end date is not after its start date.

checks.title: No balances configured
checks.description: The scenario configures no starting balances.

checks.title: No balance in the symbol's currencies
checks.description: None of the configured balances is in the base or the quote currency of the symbol.

checks.title: Account currency not in the symbol
checks.description: The configured account currency is neither the base nor the quote currency of the symbol; settling in a third currency is not supported.

checks.title: Account currency set to the quote
checks.description: At spot the account currency was changed to the quote currency, because spot settles in the quote currency and a base-currency profit would mix units.

checks.title: Invalid parameter
checks.description: A decision logic or worker parameter is unknown, missing, or outside its declared range.

checks.title: Data requirements could not be computed
checks.description: Working out which bars and how much warmup the workers need failed with an error.

checks.title: Worker does not fit the market
checks.description: A worker needs an activity measure (such as traded volume) that the broker's market does not provide.

checks.title: Subscribed worker output does not exist
checks.description: The decision logic subscribes to a worker output that the worker does not produce.

checks.title: Algorithm state cannot be saved
checks.description: The decision logic keeps state across sessions, but its state cannot be written as JSON.

checks.title: Algorithm reads the system clock
checks.description: The decision logic or a worker reads the system clock instead of the run's own clock, which makes a backtest impossible to reproduce.

checks.title: Algorithm not recommended for this market
checks.description: The decision logic names the markets or instruments it is meant for, and this one is not among them.

checks.title: Broker configuration unavailable
checks.description: The broker's configuration could not be fetched or loaded.

checks.title: Symbol not in the broker configuration
checks.description: The broker configuration does not list the symbol.

checks.title: Swap mode not modelled
checks.description: The symbol charges overnight swap in a way the simulation does not model.

checks.title: Symbol specification fetched long ago
checks.description: The backtest read a symbol's minimums and steps from a cache entry older than its refresh interval; the venue may have changed them since.

checks.title: No data coverage report
checks.description: No coverage report exists for the broker and symbol, so the scenario's window cannot be checked against the data.

checks.title: Data does not cover the window
checks.description: The scenario's window starts before the first tick or ends after the last one.

checks.title: Start inside a data gap
checks.description: The scenario starts inside a gap in the tick data.

checks.title: Gap in the tick data
checks.description: The tick data has a gap inside the scenario's window that is longer than allowed.

checks.title: Not enough warmup bars
checks.description: A timeframe has fewer bars complete at the scenario's first tick than its indicators need to settle, because the archive holds no more; the scenario runs and says so.

checks.title: No warmup bars
checks.description: A timeframe the workers read has not a single bar complete at the scenario's first tick, so its indicators would start from nothing; the scenario is refused.

checks.title: Warmup larger than the bar history
checks.description: A worker requires more bars than the renderer keeps per timeframe (bar_max_history), so its history would be cut short at the start; the scenario is refused.

checks.title: No tick data loaded
checks.description: No tick data could be loaded for the scenario.

checks.title: Data origin not admitted
checks.description: The scenario read data files whose origin is not on the admitted list.

checks.title: Signal data unavailable
checks.description: The signal data the scenario binds could not be loaded.

checks.title: Spread of the ticks without a quote unavailable
checks.description: The scenario reads ticks that recorded no quote and models their spread, but the day estimates it is priced from could not be built; the scenario is refused rather than run without a spread.

checks.title: Signal data thin in the window
checks.description: The scenario's signal source has little or patchy data in its window; the scenario still runs.

checks.title: Gap in the signal data
checks.description: The signal data has a gap inside the scenario's window.

checks.title: Stress test names a source the scenario lacks
checks.description: A planned data outage names a data source the scenario does not read.

checks.title: Refused before it ran
checks.description: The scenario was refused right before it would have started, for the reason stated.

checks.title: Debug mode
checks.description: The run executed serially under a debugger, so its timings are not representative.

checks.title: Stress test active
checks.description: At least one unit ran with a stress test that injects errors and rejections on purpose.

checks.title: Real orders from uncommitted code
checks.description: A session trading real orders was started with --allow-dirty from code that is not exactly one commit.

checks.title: Open positions continued under a changed configuration
checks.description: A start declared --accept-composite-change and continued what the venue still held under another composite than the one that opened it.

checks.title: Configuration not compared with the carry-over
checks.description: The session took over what the venue still held without being able to compare its configuration with the one that opened it.

checks.title: Drawdown and risk baseline started fresh
checks.description: The session did not continue the drawdown curve and the risk baseline its carry-over held: a rehearsal wrote them and the session placed real orders, or the other way round, or the carry-over does not say which.

checks.title: Code not under version control
checks.description: A component was loaded from a directory that git does not track or cannot read, so the run cannot name the code it ran.

checks.title: Data format version unknown
checks.description: Some data files the run read carry no format version in the tick index.

checks.title: Data origin not stamped
checks.description: Some data files the run read carry no origin stamped by their producer, so they are usable but cannot enter a parity comparison.

checks.title: External data read
checks.description: Some data files the run read, or the bars a warmup history started from, are a venue's published history rather than our own collection; such ticks are never admissible for a parity comparison.

checks.title: Ticks without a quote
checks.description: Some tick files the run read carry no quote (bid equals ask as recorded), so no spread was measured on them; what a backtest charged there instead is the modelled spread.

checks.title: Modelled spread on ticks without a quote
checks.description: A backtest gave its ticks without a quote the quote the spread estimated for the previous day implies, so its fills, marks and stops crossed a modelled spread there; the count says how many such ticks were given one and at what median, factor and estimator version.

checks.title: Ticks without an arrival time
checks.description: Some tick files the run read record no receive time, so tick timing falls back to the event time.

checks.title: Arrival time reconstructed
checks.description: Some tick files the run read carry an arrival time that was reconstructed after the fact rather than recorded on arrival.

checks.title: Trades missing from the data
checks.description: Some tick files the run read miss more of the venue's trades than reconnect noise explains.

checks.title: Synthetic signal data
checks.description: Some signal data the run read is generated rather than a market record.

checks.title: Several account currencies
checks.description: The run mixes account currencies; profit and loss is shown per currency and never added across them.

checks.title: Order-event stream lacks submissions
checks.description: The order-event stream holds fewer submissions than the executor counted — a record was lost, most likely to a failed write — so the counters derived from it are too low.

checks.title: Scenarios far apart in time
checks.description: The scenarios of one currency span many days, so their combined profit and loss is a statistic, not a portfolio.

checks.title: Processing slower than the ticks arrive
checks.description: In some scenarios a tick takes longer to process, on average, than the shortest gaps between ticks; a tick processing budget would simulate the ticks a live run would skip.

checks.title: Budget below data resolution
checks.description: The tick processing budget is below one millisecond, which the data cannot resolve, so it has no effect.

checks.title: Budget skips ticks needlessly
checks.description: The tick processing budget is more than twice the usual processing time, so ticks are skipped that a live run would have processed.

checks.title: Ticks arrived while the last was processing
checks.description: More ticks than the configured share arrived while the previous one was still being processed, so those decisions ran on data that was already old.

checks.title: High coordination overhead
checks.description: Coordinating the workers and the decision logic costs more than half of their own computation in some scenarios.

checks.title: Infrastructure dominates the cost
checks.description: An operation outside the trading logic is the largest cost in many scenarios.

checks.title: Parallel workers cost time
checks.description: Running the workers in parallel was slower than running them one after another.

checks.title: Parameters differ across windows
checks.description: The strategy parameters are not the same in every window, so comparing in-sample with out-of-sample is not a fair test.

checks.title: Too few windows
checks.description: The robustness figures rest on fewer windows than the configured minimum.

checks.title: Expectancy not measured in some windows
checks.description: Some windows have no trade with an R, so the metric has no value there and no verdict is given. A logic keeping its own exits has none; use another metric.

checks.title: Block splitting distorts the windows
checks.description: Splitting the data into blocks distorted the windows beyond the trust limit, so no verdict is given.

checks.title: Too few in- or out-of-sample windows
checks.description: The in-sample or the out-of-sample group has fewer windows than the minimum, so no verdict is given.

checks.title: Overfit
checks.description: Out-of-sample results fall sharply below in-sample results: the strategy is likely fitted to the in-sample windows.

checks.title: Release certificate expired
checks.description: The newest certificate of a release gate is past its validity date, so the gate has to be run again before a release.

checks.title: Fee structure frozen long ago
checks.description: A broker's declared fee rates were frozen more than ninety days ago; the venue may charge this account differently by now.
